hints: Choose downward as positive so that the displacement and gravitational acceleration have the same sign.
Use the constant-acceleration equation linking initial speed, final speed and displacement; no time value is needed.
Rearrange v² = u² + 2as to find u² using v = 8.7 m s⁻¹, a = 9.81 m s⁻² and s = 1.5 m.
walkthrough: Take downward as the positive direction. The ball has displacement s = 1.5 m and acceleration a = +9.81 m s⁻².
Use v² = u² + 2as with final speed v = 8.7 m s⁻¹.
u = √46.26 = 6.80 m s⁻¹, so the initial speed is 6.8 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses v² = u² + 2as and rearranges with the 1.5 m downward displacement and gravitational acceleration.
Obtains an initial downward speed of 6.8 m s⁻¹.

hints: Identify the two bodies in contact and name the force each exerts on the other.
Newton's third-law forces form an interaction pair, so they act on different objects rather than cancelling on one object.
Compare the pair in both magnitude and direction: force of ground on ball, and force of ball on ground.
walkthrough: During contact, the ground exerts a force on the ball and the ball exerts a force on the ground.
These forces are a Newton's third-law pair, so they have equal magnitudes.
They act in opposite directions: the force on the ball by the ground is opposite to the force on the ground by the ball.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the force exerted by the ground on the ball equals the force exerted by the ball on the ground in magnitude.
States that the two interaction forces act in opposite directions.

hints: Momentum has direction, so assign signs before finding its change through the rebound.
For example, take upward as positive: the incoming ball has a negative velocity and the rebounding ball has a positive velocity.
Use Δp = m(v_after − v_before) with m = 0.059 kg, v_after = +5.4 m s⁻¹ and v_before = −8.7 m s⁻¹.
walkthrough: Take upward as positive. Before the collision, v_before = −8.7 m s⁻¹; after it rebounds, v_after = +5.4 m s⁻¹.
The momentum change is Δp = m(v_after − v_before).
The magnitude of the change in momentum is 0.83 N s.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses p = mv for an incoming or rebounding momentum with the 0.059 kg mass and a stated speed.
Accounts for the reversal of direction and obtains a momentum-change magnitude of 0.83 N s.

hints: Average resultant force is determined by how quickly the ball's momentum changes during contact.
Use the momentum-change magnitude from part (c)(i) and the 0.091 s contact time.
Calculate F = Δp / Δt = 0.83 / 0.091.
walkthrough: The average resultant force is the rate of change of momentum: F = Δp / Δt.
The collision changes the ball's momentum by 0.83 N s in 0.091 s.
The magnitude of the average resultant force is 9.1 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Divides the 0.83 N s momentum change by the 0.091 s collision time to obtain 9.1 N.

hints: The average resultant force found in part (c)(ii) is not the contact force alone, because weight also acts on the ball.
During the rebound, the ground force is upward and the ball's weight is downward; find the weight from its mass.
Use F_resultant = F_ground − W, then rearrange for F_ground.
walkthrough: During the collision, the ground exerts an upward force on the ball while the ball's weight acts downward.
The weight is W = mg = 0.059 × 9.81 = 0.579 N, approximately 0.58 N.
Taking upward as positive, the resultant force is F_ground − W = 9.1 N.
F_ground = 9.1 + 0.58 = 9.68 N, so the average force exerted by the ground is 9.7 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the ball's weight as 0.059 × 9.81, approximately 0.58 N.
Adds the downward 0.58 N weight to the 9.1 N upward resultant force to obtain a ground force of 9.7 N.

hints: The vertical axis is speed, so it cannot be negative even though the ball moves downward.
With negligible air resistance, the ball's acceleration and hence the speed–time gradient are constant.
The ball is already thrown with a non-zero speed at t = 0; draw a straight rising line from that point to t = T.
walkthrough: At t = 0 the ball already has speed u, so the graph starts above zero on the speed axis.
Air resistance is negligible, so the acceleration due to gravity is constant.
A constant positive acceleration gives a straight speed–time graph with positive gradient.
Draw that straight line from the non-zero speed at t = 0 to the vertical line at t = T.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a straight line of positive gradient that begins at non-zero speed at t = 0 and ends at t = T.

hints: On a speed–time graph, the gradient represents the magnitude of acceleration while the ball continues downward.
As the ball speeds up, consider how the upward air-resistance force changes compared with the constant downward weight.
Link the changing resultant force to acceleration, then state what happens to the graph's gradient over time.
walkthrough: As the ball's downward speed increases, the upward air resistance increases.
Its weight remains constant, so the increasing air resistance reduces the downward resultant force.
The ball's downward acceleration therefore decreases with time.
The gradient of the speed–time graph decreases with time, so the graph becomes progressively less steep.

ai_rubric.observable: States that air resistance increases as the ball's speed increases.
Explains that the resultant force and acceleration decrease, so the speed–time graph's gradient decreases with time.
